record.original_question: Let M̃ be the one-dimensional uncentered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, and let BV(R) denote the Banach space of functions f : R -> R of bounded total variation with norm ||f||_{BV(R)} = |f(-infinity)| + Var(f). Is the map M̃ : BV(R) -> BV(R) continuous?

evidence.quote: The uncentered maximal function is defined analogously, taking the supremum of averages over open balls that contain the point x, but that are not necessarily centered at x.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})$ denote the Banach space of functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ of bounded total variation, equipped with the norm
$$\|f\|_{\mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})} = |f(-\infty)| + \mathrm{Var}(f),$$
where $f(-\infty) = \lim_{x\to-\infty} f(x)$ and $\mathrm{Var}(f)$ is the total variation of $f$ on $\mathbb{R}$.

Let $\widetilde{M}$ denote the one-dimensional uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator, defined for a locally integrable function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ by
$$\widetilde{M}f(x) = \sup_{I\ni x} \frac{1}{|I|}\int_I |f(y)|\,dy,$$
where the supremum is taken over all bounded open intervals $I\subset\mathbb{R}$ containing $x$.

It is known that $\widetilde{M}$ maps $\mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})$ into itself boundedly. Determine whether the map
$$\widetilde{M} : \mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})$$
is continuous.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was solved affirmatively by C. González-Riquelme and D. Kosz in "BV continuity for the uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator," Journal of Functional Analysis 281 (2021), Article 109037, who proved that the map $\widetilde{M}:\mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})\to\mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})$ is continuous.

status_evidence.title: BV continuity for the uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator
status_evidence.snippet: BV continuity for the uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator, J. Funct. Anal. 281 (2021) 109037, by González-Riquelme and Kosz.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes that the uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator is continuous from BV(R) to BV(R).
